manage crisis situations such as delay in flight take-off, delay in landing, diversion of flights etc.
Further, training should also be given to the airlines staff to sensitize them to meet the needs
of persons with disability. Intensive training should be given to the crew and staff to extend
courteous and decent behaviour to the passengers. The crew should be trained to be more polite
than saying 'please' or 'thank you'. The passengers expect a civilized behaviour from the cabin
crew and the ground staff as the salaries to the cabin crew and ground staff are paid from the
income earned from the passengers. (Para 17)
The Committee notes that the training modules, training schedules, content of training,
duration of training, budget allocation for training etc. varies from airline to airline. In some of
the cases, the training programmes are non-existent or just for namesake. The Government
should come up with a training programme suitable to Indian conditions emphasizing on courteous
behaviour to the passengers. The Committee underlines the need to standardise the training
programmes of all the airlines. The Committee recommends that the Government should formulate
the guidelines for such training programmes applicable to all the airlines, at the earliest.
(Para 18)
The Committee notes that the check-in process and collection of luggage are cumbersome
and time consuming. What the passenger wants is a quick check-in, without long queues and a
smooth process of security check. Despite the huge claims of airlines regarding the check-in
process, the Committee is compelled to observe that the check-in counters are in a mess,
especially those of the low cost airlines such as IndiGo. (Para 20)
The Committee has noticed reports of some private airlines creating long queues at the
check-in counters to delay the process of check-in so that passengers miss their scheduled
flights. This compels them to buy tickets at exorbitant prices to travel in the next available
flight. The Committee also notes that airlines are overbooking flights and creating later, artificial
situations to deny boarding to the confirmed ticket holders. Many a times it has been noticed
that adequate number of personnel are not posted to man the check-in counters. (Para 21)
The Committee recommends that arrangements be made to ensure that the passenger does
not spend more than 10 minutes in a queue at the check-in counter to get a boarding pass.
Whenever there is a rush of passengers, additional staff should be deputed at the check-in
counters. AAI and other airport operators may provide adequate number of check-in counters
and self checking kiosks at the airports. The Government should also ensure that if a passenger
is denied boarding due to rush at the counter or due to overbooking, the passenger may be
compensated adequately and he/she may be sent in an alternative flight. (Para 22)
The Committee takes note of the steps taken by the Airport operators to provide e-boarding
facility at certain airports to reduce waiting time for baggage check-in and security clearance.
The Committee desires that e-boarding facility should be made available to passengers at all
airports. (Para 25)

14
The Committee was informed that there are great difficulties in getting water and food in
low cost airlines especially in IndiGo. In IndiGo, the food has to be pre-booked and on board,
if someone demands food, they refuse to provide the food even to those who are diabetic or
suffering from other medical conditions. A passenger has to report to the airport counter 2 hours
before the departure time and one has to spend a few more hours in the flight without food and
water and it is a horrible thing to face. The Committee, therefore, recommends that IndiGo and
other low cost airlines should take adequate steps to ensure that food is available to the passengers
on demand, especially to those who are having some medical conditions. (Para 27)
The Committee notes that the main difference between a low cost carrier and the full cost
carrier is the serving of food. It is unacceptable for airlines to serve unsatisfactory food after
having charged customers for it. Every airline should maintain the highest quality of food and
they should also change the menu occasionally instead of keeping a cold sandwich in their menu
throughout the year. The Committee recommends that random audits of the catering kitchens
should be held to ensure quality, quantity and hygiene and that feedback from customers may
also be taken into account. The cost of food may be separately printed on the ticket.
(Para 28)
 Due to their profit motive, the airlines are not providing adequate leg space to the passengers.
The Committee desires that the Ministry of Civil Aviation may prepare a guideline laying down
a minimum space standard in respect of seats and leg room. (Para 29)
The Committee has been informed by all airlines that no unserviceable seats are being
offered to passengers. However, the Committee has noted that unserviceable seats are in fact
offered to passengers and complaints made to the cabin crew in this regard have gone unheeded.
The Committee noticed that though all the airlines have a policy of not offering unserviceable
seats, the practice is that these are silently offered to the unsuspecting passengers. It is a cruel
joke to offer unserviceable seats even to Business Class passengers. Due to their busy schedule,
the passengers are compelled to travel by availing the unserviceable seats. The Committee
observes that it is a deficiency of service by service airlines. The airlines should take an initiative
to ensure that unserviceable seats are either replaced or repaired at the earliest. Monetary
compensation may be given to the affected passengers who are offered the unserviceable seats.
The Government should formulate a policy to restrict the use of unserviceable seats.
(Para 31)
The Committee notes that cancellation charges levied by private airlines are arbitrarily set.
There is no uniformity or minimum standards to impose charges for rescheduling, cancellation
and no-show. Attractive offers by private airlines veil the fact that passengers are charged the
entire ticket amount if they want to cancel the tickets. The airlines must be restricted to
charging not more than 50% of the base fare as cancellation charges. The tax and fuel surcharge
collected should be refunded to the passengers on cancellation of tickets. The Committee desires
that DGCA may conduct periodic checks to ensure that the cancellation charges are not a burden
on consumers. (Para 40)

15
The cancellation charges may be printed prominently in the ticket itself and not as a fine
print. Norms for cancellation should be given more publicity through posters and websites.
(Para 41)
Therefore, the Committee recommends the Ministry to reissue guidelines reiterating already
existing guidelines, hence ensuring strict compliance by all the airlines. If needed, the schemes
and guidelines may be strengthened for the smooth travel of differentlyabled persons.
(Para 42)
The Committee notes that even after the existence of guidelines of BCAS, there are
instances of misbehaviour by CISF and other security personnel. The Committee observes that
the Government needs to be proactive to face the emerging challenges of the growth of Civil
Aviation Sector. The recent incidents of misbehaviour definitely show CISF in poor light and
prove that the training programmes are insufficient and more needs to be done. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that the Government should reevaluate the soft skill training programmes
of CISF and security personnel and motivate them to be passenger friendly. (Para 44)
Poor experiences in the toilets are often very strongly linked to passengers' overall
satisfaction. Having enough washrooms in the right places and keeping the washrooms clean
should be the priority of the AAI and Airport operators. The toilets should be the statement of
quality. The Committee recommends that cleanliness should be given utmost importance by AAI
and various other airport operators and they should take effective steps to ensure that toilets
at the airports should be maintained in a clean and tidy manner. The Government of India should
also monitor the quality of the toilets of all the airports. (Para 46)
The Ministry of Civil Aviation has developed an Air Sewa Application which can be availed
through Web portals and mobile phones, with an aim to help the air travellers. It contains a
module for receiving, tracking and monitoring of grievances with the stakeholders. Around
20,000 people downloaded this application and the Ministry has received 6,000 complaints from
passengers during the last year. The Committee is surprised to note that in a country where
there are more than 16 crores passengers using air services, just 20,000 people are using the
application developed by the Civil Aviation Ministry. It should be improved and the App may be
advertised to ensure that every passenger is aware of the existence of the App. Every grievance
redressal mechanism of the Airlines may be integrated with the Air Sewa App of the Government
so that better monitoring can be done. (Para 48)
During the deliberations of the Committee, the CEO, Jet Airways was requested to address
the issue of customer complaints. The Committee also notes, through personal anecdotes of
Committee Members, the deliberate reluctance of Jet Airways to note customer complaints. The
Committee is of the view that a proper complaints redressal mechanism should be in place with
all airlines. The complaints received from the customers should be redressed in a time bound
manner. It should be ensured that the complaints have been redressed to the satisfaction of the
customers. The details of the complaint redressal mechanism should be adequately advertised
and printed bold in the tickets of the airlines. (Para 49)

16
The Committee notes that the officials at the immigration counters have no right to be rude
and discourteous. They are just Government servants regulated by the set of rules and regulations.
Their main role is to facilitate the passenger's journey and not to misbehave. The Committee
recommends that soft skills training be imparted to the persons at immigration counters given
their direct dealings with foreign tourists. (Para 51)
The Committee is aware that airport infrastructure has a major role to play in extending
amenities and conveniences to the passengers. The Committee is of the view that there is a need
for adequate technology driven infrastructure in our country to enable airlines to improve their
on-time performance. (Para 54)
The Committee realizes that so far, the growth of airport infrastructure has not been
commensurate with the growth in the number of passengers. Keeping in view the pace at which
Indian aviation is growing, the Committee recommends that AAI and other Airport Operators
should bolster their efforts to build new infrastructure and to expand existing airports to enhance
the facilities available at airports. Decongesting the airports, decongesting the runway and the
airspace should be the top priority of the Government. Airport facilities need to be upgraded on
an urgent basis. (Para 55)
The Committee notes that due to 'non-uniform block time', the passengers often have to
spend more time on board the aircraft. The practice of 'non-uniform block time' is obviously not
desirable. The Committee, therefore, recommends that all the airlines may follow uniform block
time. The Committee also recommends that a co-ordinated effort should be made by Air Traffic
Control, Airports Authority of India, Airport operators and Airlines for maintaining punctuality
in air services. (Para 57)
The Committee notes that in granting traffic rights, home carriers' interests, whether
Government owned or private, are always considered. The incremental capacity generated by the
bilateral could not be used by the home carriers due to the limitation of non-availability of
landing slots and parking slots in foreign destinations. The Government which is aware of the
limitations, knowingly and willingly, allowed incremental capacity to foreign airlines whereas the
home carriers are left in a lurch. The Committee, therefore, recommends that all bilateral rights
may be directly linked with the slots being given to the Indian carriers in foreign destinations.
The Committee recommends that the Ministry should thoroughly examine this issue of making
slots available to the Indian airlines and ensure that airlines of India get fair allocations.
(Para 60)
The Committee is of the view that the airlines should strike the right balance between profit
making and social responsibility. The Committee, therefore, appreciates the various CSR initiatives
undertaken by airlines and expects that they should do more. (Para 61)
The Committee notes with dismay that the Government has adopted the open sky policy
without laying down the necessary guidelines, rules and regulations to control the activities of
the airlines. The consumers are at the receiving end and at the mercy of the private airlines for

17
any kind of services. The Committee is not clear who fixes the standards and what are the
standards, be it training, quality of food, amenities to passengers, behaviour of airlines staff,
quality of seats, cancellation charges, pricing of air tickets etc. The Committee desires that the
Government should wake up from its slumber and perform their duties to save the airline
passengers from the vices and to make the air travel an enjoyable experience for them. Civil
Aviation and Airlines industry is service industry and any service industry has to be user friendly
and customer friendly. (Para 62)

REPORT
The Ministry of Civil Aviation is responsible for the formulation of national policies and programmes
for the development and regulation of the Civil Aviation sector in the country. It is responsible for the
administration of the Aircraft Act, 1934, Aircraft Rules, 1937 and various other legislations pertaining to
the aviation sector in the country.
2. In addition to the primary functions of framing of policies, the Ministry provides guidance to
the organizations in the implementation of policy guidelines, monitors and evaluates their activities and
also provides their interface with Parliament. It also supervises implementation by the organizations
of special programmes of the Government, particularly those intended for the weaker sections of
society.
3. The Ministry of Civil Aviation has the following or ganizations under its administrative control:—
(i) Attached Offices /Organizations
• Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA)
• Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS)
• Commission of Railway Safety (CRS)
• Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB)
(ii) Autonomous Bodies
• Indira Gandhi Rashtriya Uran Akademi (IGRUA)
• Airports Economic Regulatory Authority (AERA)
• Rajiv Gandhi National Aviation University (RGNAU)
(iii) Public Sector Undertakings
• Airports Authority of India (AAI)
• Air India Limited (AIL)
• Pawan Hans Limited (PHL)

Culture considered Demand No.9 containing the details of budget allocations of the Ministry of Civil

of Civil Aviation as well as the Heads of the organizations under its purview, on budgetary and other
aspects.

20. The Ministry, in its written reply, has stated that in cases of delayed infusion of equity, the company
has to resort to increased bank borrowings to meet its shortfall of funds requirement. Even in such case,
bank borrowings are not forthcoming without adequate assurance/guarantee from the Government since
the company is under FRP and its borrowings are totally guided by its Consortium of Lenders. The
second option for the company is to defer some creditor payments so that funds can be used to meet
its day to day operational requirements. In both the cases, the company has to take a financial hit because
of increased interest outgo either by way of increased bank borrowings or by way of deferment of
various creditor payments.

23. The Committee observes that the shortfall in Equity Infusion in 2017-18 was to the tune
of ````` 468.52 crores. The Committee is of the view that such shortfall adversely impacts the
financial and operational performance of the company as the same creates liquidity issues for
the company whereby the company is unable to meet its financial commitments and to maintain
its the operational efficiency. The Committee, therefore, is of the considered view that such
short-fall, at this stage when the company is presently placed at a critical position in achieving
the TAP targets, should be avoided. Since the committed financial support from the Government
is vital to sustain the momentum of performance of Air India, the Committee strongly recommends
that the full amount of equity infusion should be restored to Air India. The Committee further
recommends that the Ministry of Civil Aviation may take up this matter with the Ministry of
Finance for the restoration of the full amount of Equity Infusion.

36. GREEN INITIATIVES TAKEN UP BY AAI
1. Solar Power Plants:- AAI is setting up the solar power plants for energy generation at various
airports in place of conventional source of fuel i.e. coal etc., which is non-renewable type and
also causes pollution.
In line with the above, AAI has signed MoU with Solar Corporation of India (SECI) to set
up the roof top Solar Power Plant at various airports and also providing Ground Mounted Solar
Power Plant through open tender.

23
AAI has commissioned 27.99 MWp Solar Power Plant at Airports by which AAI has generated
289 lakhs units till December'2017 and reduced approximately 260 Metric Ton of Carbon
emission.Total 3.67 MWp capacity roof top and ground mounted Solar Plant installation works
are in progress.
2. Sewage Treatment Plants:- AAI has set up sewage treatment plants at airports for management
of waste disposal and for use of the treated recycled water for the gardening purpose, for
flushing in toilets and also used in the HV AC system to minimize the use of fresh water. Sludge
as a final product with water is used in the gardening as compost/fertilizer. Through this
process AAI is trying to minimize the pollution of natural water bodies and also conserve on
consumption of water.
3. Use of Acoustic Enclosure type DG sets:- To minimize the sound pollution as per the norms
set up by the CPCB, AAI is using only canopy type DG sets at the airports.
4. To reduce dust generation and air pollution at construction sites in airports, wheel washing and
water sprinklers are being used.
5. Extensive landscaping with horticulture and tree plantation.
6. Set up of Automatic Organic Composters.
37. The Committee realizes that so far, the growth of airport infrastructure has not been
commensurate with the growth in the number of passengers and the huge growth in civil aviation
sector. Keeping in view the pace at which Indian aviation is growing, the Committee recommends
that AAI and other Airport Operators should bolster their efforts to build new infrastructure and
to expand existing airports to enhance the facilities available at airports. Decongesting the
airports, decongesting the runway and the airspace should be the top priority of the Government.
Airport facilities need to be upgraded on an urgent basis. While constructing new airports, a
futuristic plan keeping pace with the growth in the Civil Aviation sector is needed.

Airlines. Subsequently it was decided to make it,self reliant and M/s. CAE was awarded a Management

year. For the first three years of contract (FY 08-09 to FY10-11) Government provided subsidy @
` 6.80 crores per annum.

42 (Multi engine ) aircraft. Post signing of the CAE Management Contract, the engine manufacturer
company, M/s. Thielert went bankrupt and IGRUA had to procure aircraft with petrol Engines.

being operated successfully as DA 40 NG and DA 42NG (multi engine) aircraft. These aircraft have been
certified by EASA, FAA and DGCA.
48. Nine aircraft on IGRUA inventory (5 TB 20 and 4 Zlin) are expected to retire within two years as
they would have completed their technical life.
49. In addition to the replacement of nine retiring aircraft, IGRUA plans to procure six more diesel
powered aircraft to obtain maximum utilisation of assets available at IGRUA. This would also help
IGRUA become self reliant with a lower course fee.
50. IGRUA business plan envisage replacing its entire existing fleet of 24 aircraft with aircraft fitted
diesel engine. In addition it is proposed to purchase 6 additional diesel engine aircraft, so that the facilities
and huge infrastructure available at IDRUA is put to maximum use. This will not only result in reduction
in cost of training but also help IGRUDA in becoming free.

EXORBITANT AIRFARES
104. The Committee notes that around festivals and for bookings made closer to the date of travel, some
airlines are charging more than ten times of the advance booking fare.
105. The Ministry, in its written reply, has stated that Under Aircraft Rules, 135 the provision of
prevailing airfares, are neither fixed nor regulated by the Government:
(a) Under the provision of Sub Rule (1) of Rule 135 of the Aircraft Rules, 1937 every air transport
undertaking engaged in scheduled air services require to establish tariff having regard to all
relevant factors, including cost of operation, characteristic of services, reasonable profit and
the generally prevailing staff.
(b) The airfares so established by the airline are required to be displayed on their respective
websites under the provision of Sub-Rule (2) 135 of Aircraft Rules, 1937.
(c) The airlines remain complaint to the prevailing regulation as long as fares charged by them are
in line with fare displayed on their website.
106. DGCA randomly monitors the fare to ensure that the fare being charged is not beyond the established
tariff displayed on their websites. In the event of a natural disaster or calamity, when fares seem to move
upwards, DGCA asks the airlines not to exploit the situation and charge fares within their established
tariff.
107. The Committee, in its earlier Reports, had recommended that the Ministry should take
effective steps to control the surge in airfares. The Committee feels that the Ministry has not
given serious thought and deliberation to the recommendations of the Committee.
108. The Committee also notes that even after 50% reduction of the ATF prices over a period
of time, the airlines have not passed on the benefit of reduction in ATF prices to the consumers.
The Committee recommends that the Ministry should take effective steps to ensure that the
airlines pass on the benefit to the travelers by reducing the air fares and inform the Committee
about the specific steps taken in this regard and the outcome thereof.
109. The Committee is of the view that the pricing mechanisms applicable in the developed
countries may not be suitable for India. The Committee believes that the Ministry of Civil
Aviation has a social responsibility towards its citizens. The Ministry, though aware of the
rampant exploitation, is not showing any proactive role in regulating the airfares. The Committee,
therefore, recommends the Ministry of Civil Aviation to consider fixing an upper limit of the air
tickets for every sector.

111. Ministry of Civil Aviation has requested Ministry of Finance to include Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF)
within the ambit of Goods and Service Tax (GST) at the earliest. It has been proposed that the GST
rate may be 5% on ATF sales to smaller aircraft (weight less than 40 tonnes), which was the pre-GST
ceiling rate of 5% V AT for "Declared Goods" status and 18% on sales to larger aircraft on par with
Aviation Gas (Avgas), another fuel solely used in the aviation sector. GST paid on ATF has been requested
to be made fully input tax creditable against the GST on output services. The Ministry has also requested
various State Governments to support this proposal. It is understood that the matter is under the
consideration of the GST Council.

or below provided to airlines operating passenger flights at RCS airports for a period of 10 years to ATF
sales to "air freighter aircraft" operating from and to RCS airports also for the same period of 10 years.

nodal Ministry for this purpose.

37
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS—AT A GLANCE
The Committee notes that ````` 6602.86 crores has been allocated for the Ministry of Civil
Aviation for 2018-19 against the allocation of ````` 2710.30 crores at RE stage in 2017-18. The
Committee desires that the Ministry may take steps to ensure that the allocated funds are
utilized fully. (Para 10)
The Committee further notes that ````` 4469.50 crores has been allocated under a new head
for the purchase of two new aircraft for Special Extra Section Flight operations. If this amount
is deducted from BE 2018-19, the remaining amount is ````` 2133.36 crores. This is lower than RE
2017-18. Keeping in view the considerable growth of the civil aviation sector, Committee is of the
considered view that with the present allocation, it would be difficult to run the existing schemes
and other activities undertaken by the Ministry. Therefore, the Committee recommends that the
Ministry should actively pursue the matter of increasing the allocation in the first supplementary
and at the RE stage in the current financial year 2018-19, with the Ministry of Finance.
(Para 10A)
The Committee notes that there is a shortfall of ````` 70.06 crores in budgetary allocation for
2018-19 on the Capital side and that the Ministry of Finance has not intimated any reason for
this reduction. Keeping in view the great surge in the civil aviation sector, Committee is of the
considered view that lack of sufficient funds should not be a reason for inadequate allocation of
funds for the vital schemes/projects of the Ministry. Therefore, the Committee recommends that
the Ministry should actively pursue the matter of increasing the allocation at the RE stage in
the current financial year 2018-19, with the Ministry of Finance. (Para 13)
The Committee takes note of the projects initiated by the Ministry during the 12th Five
Year Plan. (Para 16)
The Committee appreciates Air India for making operational profits. The Committee hopes
that Air India would register further profits in the coming months. (Para 22)
The Committee observes that the shortfall in Equity Infusion in 2017-18 was to the tune
of ````` 468.52 crores. The Committee is of the view that such shortfall adversely impacts the
financial and operational performance of the company as the same creates liquidity issues for
the company whereby the company is unable to meet its financial commitments and to maintain
its the operational efficiency. The Committee, therefore, is of the considered view that such short
fall, at this stage when the company is presently placed at a critical position in achieving the TAP
targets, should be avoided. Since the committed financial support from the Government is vital
to sustain the momentum of performance of Air India, the Committee strongly recommends that
the full amount of equity infusion should be restored to Air India. The Committee further
recommends that the Ministry of Civil Aviation may take up this matter with the Ministry of
Finance for the restoration of the full amount of Equity Infusion. (Para 23)
37

38
The Committee notes that the work has been completed at Pakyong airport. (Para 26)
The Committee is concerned about the huge amount of outstanding dues of AAI for a long
time. AAI, being the highest revenue generator, has to be actively helped by the Ministry of Civil
Aviation in this regard by taking it up with the defaulting Organizations and Ministries, including
legal recourse to recover the dues. The Committee recommends that consistent steps should be
taken by AAI to recover the outstanding dues. (Para 28)
The Committee notes that the matter is long overdue and things are delayed deliberately.
The Committee, therefore, urges upon the Ministry to ensure that the findings of the Internal
Committee may be implemented at the earliest. (Para 30)
The Committee hopes that the monetization of AAI land will generate considerable revenue
to AAI. (Para 33)
The Committee realizes that so far, the growth of airport infrastructure has not been
commensurate with the growth in the number of passengers and the huge growth in civil aviation
sector. Keeping in view the pace at which Indian aviation is growing, the Committee recommends
that AAI and other Airport Operators should bolster their efforts to build new infrastructure and
to expand existing airports to enhance the facilities available at airports. Decongesting the
airports, decongesting the runway and the airspace should be the top priority of the Government.
Airport facilities need to be upgraded on an urgent basis. While constructing new airports, a
futuristic plan keeping pace with the growth in the Civil Aviation sector is needed. (Para 37)
The Committee takes note of the allocation made for BCAS. (Para 39)
The Committee, therefore, reiterates its recommendation made in its 244th Report that the
senior positions of BCAS may be held exclusively by the cadre officials of BCAS. The Committee
further recommends that the Recruitment Rules of BCAS should be amended in such a way that
the cadre officers may, without any hindrance, be promoted up to the level of Joint Director
General. (Para 41)
The Committee notes the allocation made for DGCA. (Para 43)
The Committee desires that IGRUA may be allocated adequate funds to ensure that the
steps taken to make IGRUA self sufficient turn out to be fruitful. (Para 51)
The Committee could understand that funds are required for Pawan Hans Ltd. to replace
nine Dauphin Helicopters which are 31 years old. The Committee desires that adequate funds
should be given for the fleet replacement and augmentation of Pawan Hans Ltd. The disinvestment
of Pawan Hans may be viewed in the light of the huge jump in the profit of the company.
(Para 55)
The Committee is happy to note that the heliport at Rohini has been operationalised. The
Committee is of the view that the helicopter industry has tremendous potential to provide
services in the tourism sector, disaster management etc. The Committee desires that more such
heliports may be set up throughout the country. The Committee reiterates its earlier

39
recommendation that Air India and Pawan Hans can work together to ensure seamless travel on
hub and spokes basis- bringing passengers from smaller places to various tourist spots.
(Para 58)
The Committee feels that the development of unserved and under-served airports would
give a major boost to air connectivity to various small cities and towns. It will further given a
fillip to the economic development in these areas in terms of job creation and infrastructure
development. There should not be any unreasonable restriction on the allocation of fund to the
demands of the Ministry of Civil Aviation as the money spent will spur the overall growth of the
country especially in view of the Regional Connectivity Scheme UDAN. (Para 61)
The Committee takes note of the initiatives taken under RCS. Air connectivity is the main
mode of transport for majority of the population of North East to other parts of the country and
these States are demanding overall economic development. The Committee feels that better air
connectivity is the only solution to opening up the economy of North Eastern States. Therefore,
the Committee notes that it is very essential to give a preferential treatment to the North
Eastern States as far as air connectivity is concerned. (Para 66)
The Committee further notes that the Ministry has been steadily reducing Alliance Air
operations from Kolkata. Not a single one of the newly-acquired ATR-72 aircrafts has been
inducted in Kolkata. Bengal is the gateway to the North East, and the Committee is of the
opinion that a fleet of ATR-72 aircrafts should be introduced in Kolkata and operations should
start at the earliest. (Para 66A)
The Committee hopes that the Regional Air Connectivity Fund would stimulate growth and
development in the Civil Aviation sector. (Para 70)
The Committee hopes that the University will churn out skilled professionals in the field of
Civil Aviation. (Para 73)
The Committee desires that Bio-Metric Access Control Systems may be provided at all the
airports in order to ensure safety and security. The Committee impresses upon the Ministry that
steps should be taken to address the delays in this regard. (Para 76)
The Committee desires that proactive steps should be taken by the Ministry to address the
concerns of the employees of HCIL. (Para 78)
The Committee is aware that the construction of Headquarter to these agencies is lingering
for a long period. The Committee desires that steps should be taken by the Ministry to ensure
that the construction of the combined Headquarter building is materialized without further delay.
(Para 80)
The Committee notes that Kushinagar airport has a great potential to attract a large
number of tourists especially the Buddhist tourists who are visiting India and for overall economic
development of the surrounding region. The Committee, therefore, recommends that Government
of India should take necessary steps in co-ordination with the Government of Uttar Pradesh to
ensure that the Kushinagar airport is ready for operationalisation soon. (Para 82)

40
The Committee takes note of the progress made in the renovation work of the Calicut
airport. The Committee desires that the progress of the work may be closely monitored and that
the renovation work may be completed at the earliest. (Para 84)
The Committee notes the progress made with regard to Keshod Airport. (Para 86)
The Committee notes the progress made in respect of Jewar airport. (Para 88)
The Committee takes note of the proposals for new airports, accepted by the Government.
The Committee hopes that the construction of these airports will be taken up at the earliest.
(Para 91)
The Committee desires that the concern raised by the Member may be addressed suitably.
(Para 93)
The Committee notes that at least 2876 posts are lying vacant under various organization
of the Ministry Civil Aviation at a time when a large number of educated youths are unemployed
in our country. The Committee is of the view that the existence of vacancies will hamper the
effective functioning of the organizations. The Committee strongly feels that it is inexcusable
that vacancies exist in such vital organizations. The Committee, therefore, desires that the
Ministry should pursue the matter with UPSC and other concerned agencies so that the bottlenecks
in this regard are sorted out. The Committee further desires that the amendment of Recruitment
Rules may be completed at the earliest. The Committee also recommends that the Ministry
should take advance action anticipating the vacancies in various organizations. (Para 98)
The Committee notes that the AirSewa initiative has integrated various stakeholders in
aviation sector with whom an air traveler has to interact during the air travel. The Committee
appreciates this initiative which has been launched for the benefit of the air travelers.
(Para 103)
The Committee, in its earlier Reports, had recommended that the Ministry should take
effective steps to control the surge in airfares. The Committee feels that the Ministry has not
given serious thought and deliberation to the recommendations of the Committee. (Para 107)
The Committee also notes that even after 50% reduction of the ATF prices over a period
of time, the airlines have not passed on the benefit of reduction in ATF prices to the consumers.
The Committee recommends that the Ministry should take effective steps to ensure that the
airlines pass on the benefit to the travelers by reducing the air fares and inform the Committee
about the specific steps taken in this regard and the outcome thereof. (Para 108)
The Committee is of the view that the pricing mechanisms applicable in the developed
countries may not be suitable for India. The Committee believes that the Ministry of Civil
Aviation has a social responsibility towards its citizens. The Ministry, though aware of the
rampant exploitation, is not showing any proactive role in regulating the airfares. The Committee,
therefore, recommends the Ministry of Civil Aviation to consider fixing an upper limit of the air
tickets for every sector. (Para 109)

41
The Committee takes note of the fact that a major difficulty being faced by airlines is the
high cost of ATF which is further aggravated by taxes and that due to the distortion in the price
structure caused by the taxation policies, the financial liability of airlines is getting strongly
affected. In this regard, the Committee urges that the Ministry of Finance may consider including
ATF in GST. (Para 113)
The Committee may be apprised of the reasons for not providing budgetary support for Aero
Club of India for 2018-19. (Para 115)
The Committee notes that there has been a huge jump in the number of aircrafts used for
scheduled operations by various airlines. This implies the need for more pilots in the coming
years. This can be catered to by the pilot training institutes. India needs more and more pilot
Training Institutes to train our youngsters who are presently relying on foreign countries to get
pilot training. This will save lot of foreign exchanges in many ways. The Committee desires that
the Ministry may take steps to look into the reasons for the institutes for pilot training being
non-operational and revive them. (Para 117)
The Committee desires that the Ministry should urgently intervene in this regard and sort
out the issues. (Para 119)
The Committee takes note of the growth in the Air Cargo sector. (Para 122)
Poor experiences in the toilets are often very strongly linked to passengers' overall
satisfaction. Having enough washrooms in the right places and keeping the washrooms clean
should be the priority of the AAI and other Airport operators. The Committee recommends that
cleanliness should be given utmost importance by AAI and various other airport operators and
they should take effective steps to ensure that toilets at the airports should be maintained in
a clean and tidy manner . The Government of India should also monitor the quality of the toilets
of all the airports. (Para 124)
The Committee notes that the officials at the immigration counters have no right to be rude
and discourteous. They are just Government servants regulated by the set of rules and regulations.
Their main role is to facilitate the passenger's journey and not to misbehave. The Committee
recommends that soft skills training be imparted to the persons at immigration counters given
their direct dealings with foreign tourists. (Para 126)
The Committee desires that the Ministry should address this issue urgently. (Para 128)
The Committee feels that an effective co-ordination mechanism among the Ministries of
Culture, Tourism, Civil Aviation and Road Transport & Highways is needed in order to ensure
that the places of tourist and cultural importance are integrated seamlessly with well connected
roads and airports. Such a mechanism would ensure that the tourists are provided with required
facilities like budget hotels, taxis, souvenir shops, restaurants etc. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the Ministry of Civil Aviation may co-ordinate in formulating an action plan
with the above said Ministries in this regard and that the Ministry of Tourism may be made the
nodal Ministry for this purpose. (Para 129)

REPORT
Culture plays an important role in the development agenda of any nation. It represents a set of
shared attitudes, values, goals and practices. Culture and creativity manifest themselves in almost all
economic, social and other activities. India is a vast and diverse country with a rich cultural heritage that
has been widely appreciated all over the world.
2. The Ministry of Culture is mandated the functions like preservation and conservation of our
cultural heritage and promotion of all forms of art and culture, both tangible and intangible. The Ministry's
task is to develop and sustain ways and means through which the creative and aesthetic sensibilities of
the people remain active and dynamic. The functional spectrum of this Ministry is wide, ranging from
generating cultural awareness at grassroots level to promoting cultural exchanges at international level.
Gandhian Heritage and Convocation of important historical events and centenaries of great personalities
are also the responsibility of Ministry of Culture.
3. The Ministry is the custodian of all the major libraries in the country and through National Archives
of India, it is responsible for maintenance of all archival records of the country. The Ministry also
protects and promotes Buddhist and Tibetan Culture. Capacity building programme in the field of Indian
art and culture is promoted through institutions like School of Archaeology, School of Archives, National
Museum, Institute of History of Art Conservation and Museology, Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of
Asian Studies, National School of Drama, Kalakshetra Foundation. On the international front, the Ministry
is responsible for implementing te various UNESCO conventions and for entering into Cultural Exchange
Agreements with partnering countries.

CELLULAR JAIL IN PORT BLAIR
44. The Ministry, in its written reply, has stated that the Cellular Jail in Port Blair figured in the
tentative list of UNESCO but Andaman and Nicobar administration has no information of preparation of
the nomination dossier on Cellular Jail for submission to the World Heritage Centre for its inclusion in
the World Heritage List of UNESCO.
45. The Committee is distressed to note that despite its repeated recommendations to include
the Cellular Jail in Port Blair in the World Heritage List of UNESCO, nothing concrete has been
done in this regard. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should furnish a status report
on the issue at the earliest and keeping in view of the historical importance of the Cellular Jail,
the Ministry of Culture should take proactive steps to include the Cellular Jail in Port Blair in

62. National Culture Fund (NCF) constitutes an important departure from the implementation strategies

ANTHROPOLOGICAL SURVEY OF INDIA
81. Since its inception in 1945 the Anthropological Survey of India, a premier research organization
under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India is dedicated to map the Bio-Cultural Profile of Indian
population utilizing manpower specialized in Cultural and Physical Anthropology, Human Ecology,
Psychology, Bio-chemistry, Linguistics and Folklore; developing the organization as launching pad for
technology based research to be applied in human development; understanding, documenting and preparing
database and disseminating information about bio-cultural diversity of Indian populations through published
research work, seminars, workshops, awareness programmes, outreach programmes, audio-visual
documentation, museum documentation; and development of library for facilitating research in
anthropology.
Major contributions :
• Publication of People of India Project, which provides brief socio-cultural profile on each
of the 4635 communities in India.
• Establishment of High Technology DNA Laboratories at Kolkata and Mysore.
• The Zonal Anthropological Museums (ZAM) located in different locations along with the
length and breadth of the country displays biological, Social and cultural heritage of the
country. These Museums attracts thousands of tourists, scholars and students every months.
Recent research projects of the Anthropological Survey of India:
1. Development and Sustainability
Under the project 'Development and Sustainability'16 villages have been initiated for the study. This
project aims at critically assessing the development projects in the broader framework of their
impacts and sustainability. The studies were carried out at different locations which include both
tribal and non-tribal locations and communities.
2. Bio-Cultural Diversity, Environment and Sustainable Development (Village Studies)
The study of 50 villages was undertaken to elucidate and analyse the changes with respect to
Livelihood Practices, Education, Health and Health Care Issues and Development Initiatives.
3. Man and Environment: Study of Bio-sphere Reserves
Anthropological Survey India has completed the study of all the 18 Biosphere Reserves in India.
Through this study the Anthropological Survey of India intends to understand biological and
cultural diversity as they exist in each of the biosphere reserve together with conservation ethos
embedded in socio-economic practices as pursued by the people.

25
4. DNA Polymorphism of the Contemporary Indian Populations & Ancient Skeletal
Materials
The report "Genomic Diversity of People of India" is ready for publication based on the findings
of the National Project "DNA Polymorphism in Contemporary Indian Population and Ancient
Skeletal Remains". 74 Tribal communities' blood samples were collected for DNA studies. Y-
Chromosome phylogeny and DNA analysis of these communities were also carried out.
5. Paleoanthropology
The Anthropological Survey of India has a rich ancient human skeletal repository with a wide
ranging collection of about thirty (30) human skeletal series representing a vast horizon of culture
from the late Stone Age to the historical period including the Harappan sites.
82. The Committee takes notes of the initiatives and recommends that the Ministry should
ensure that enough fund is allocated under this head and also monitor its utilization. The
Committee notes that some of the Reports of Anthropological Survey of India are ready for
publication. The Committee recommends that the Reports may be revaluated with the help of
experts to ensure that wrong findings are rectified. The Ministry should also have a mechanism
in place to verify the reports submitted under various projects of Anthropological Survey of

89. The Committee has noticed that the persons working as guides mostly give explanation
and details of the monuments based on wrong and baseless information, many a times such
information are misleading also. This may be due to ignorance or deliberate action. The Committee
is aware that every monument has its own history and importance based on scientific and historic
facts. The tourist who visit the monuments should be given correct information by the guides.
The Committee, therefore, recommends that there should be skilled guides in the monuments
and museums and strict guidelines for giving licenses to such guides should be followed to
maintain credibility of information given to public and unauthorized guides should not be allowed
to such places. The Committee recommends that proper documentation and maintenance of data
in every site/ museum of the country is essential and should be strived for.

27
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS — AT A GLANCE
ASSESSMENT OF THE DEMANDS FOR GRANTS (2018-19) OF THE MINISTRY
The Committee is distressed to note that against a projection of ````` 3156.23 crore at RE
2017-18 an amount of Rs 2666.94 crore as ceiling of RE 2017-18 was allocated by the Ministry
of Finance which is a further reduction from budgetary allocation at BE 2017-18. The Committee
notes with dismay that though the Ministry of Culture has demanded more allocation at RE stage
in 2017-18 for works including the preservation of monuments, the Ministry of Finance reduced
the allocation which is a clear indication that the Government is giving least priority to the
activities of Ministry of Culture. (Para 8)
MINISTRY'S PROJECTED DEMAND vis-a-vis Budgetary Allocation
The Committee notes that the budgetary allocation for 2018-19 has been marginally increased
by 3.83% more than the budgetary provisions at BE 2017-18 which is not an increase at all
considering the inflation. This Committee is unhappy to note that Culture has not been given
duek attention and totally ignored by the Government. The allocated amount is short by ````` 999.7
crore against the projected amount. The Committee was informed by the Ministry that due to
the cut in the allocation the functioning of ASI and various museums may be affected. The
Committee recommends that the Ministry should pursue for an increase in budget allocation
during RE 2018-19 as the activities undertaken by the Ministry of Culture are very crucial in
maintaining the cultural identity of the nation by highlighting and preserving its rich cultural
heritage. (Para 11)
12TH FIVE YEAR PLAN
The Committee takes note of the expenditure made by the Ministry of Culture under the
Plan and Non Plan heads. The Committee observes that there has been underutilisaiton to the
tune of ````` 1046 crores under the Plan head since 2012-13. Underutilisation definitetly shows
inefficiency on the part of the Ministry. The Committee may be apprised of the hindrances in
the way of optimum expenditure. The Committee recommends the Ministry should revisit the
framework under which the expenditure was made during 12th plan to identify the reasons for
underutilisation of funds so as to avoid repetition of the mistakes in its future endeovours.
(Para 15)
In this regard, the Committee suggests that as the Ministry of Culture largely deals with
sectors of Art and Culture where outputs may not be quantified, however a progress report on
qualitative terms may be provided to the Committee. As regards a number of schemes projects/
activities where achievement are quantifiable the performance of the Ministry is very poor. It
again shows inefficiency on the part of the Ministry. The Committee recommends that the
Ministry should take every possible step to ensure that the stipulated outputs are achieved on
time. (Para 17)
27

28
AUDIT PARAS
The Committee recommends that an Inquiry Committee may be constituted to look into
the facts and circumstances which led to failure of the Ministry of Culture to fill up key posts
in National Gallery of Modern Art for over  a decade. The Committee wants to be apprised of the
current status in the matter. (Para 19)
ARCHAEOLOGICAL SURVEY OF INDIA
The Committee welcomes the initiative taken to construct boundary walls for ASI protected
monuments and removal of encroachment from centrally protected monuments/sites. The
Committee recommends that every effort should be made to construct boundary walls and
fencing to each of the 3686 nationally protected monuments in a time bound manner. The
Committee hopes that construction of boundary walls will go a long way in preventing further
encroachment of monuments. The Committee recommends that steps should be taken so that
no new encroachment takes places on such sites as removal of such encroachment is a very
cumbersome process. The Committee may also be provided a list of monuments/sites from where
encroachments have been removed. (Para 24)
The Committee is unhappy to note the delay in implementation of e-Governance in ASI
and fails to understand the delay. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should take
proactive steps to ensure that e-Governance is implemented in ASI at the earliest. The Committee
may be apprised of the action taken in this regard. (Para 26)
The Committee is happy to note the progress made in the matter of providing e-ticketing
facility in ASI protected ticketed monuments and museums as it makes it convenient for visitors
to plan their visit to the monuments in advance and help them to avoid the hassle of waiting
at the ticket counters. The Committee desires that the facility of e-ticketing may be introduced
in the remaining ASI protected monuments as well. (Para 28)
The Committee appreciates the initiative taken by the Department and hopes that in the
long run the spirit to maintain cleanliness in all the protected sites is sustained with same zeal
and enthusiasm. (Para 30)
The Committee hopes that the upgradation work in the 100 identified monuments are
completed within a fixed timeframe so that in future other monuments are identified as Adarsh
Monuments for upgradation as there is an urgent need to upgrade a large number of monuments
which are in a poor state of preservation. (Para 32)
The Committee notes that there are very few Adarsh Smaraks selected from the States
of Tamil Nadu, Kerala Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana though there exist a large
number of culturally important heritage monuments. The list of monuments identified for
upgradation as Adarsh Smarak should be inclusive so as to include monuments from every
corner of the country. (Para 33)
The Committee appreciated the measures taken by ASI for extending social security
schemes to the contractual employees and recommends that welfare measures for workers are

29
of immense importance for any organization as the country is progressing and a decent Human
Development Index needs to be achieved. (Para 35)
The Committee notes that since the rule is clear there should not be any problem in
carrying out demolition orders in future. However, the Committee recommends that Legal
Consultant at the Circle level should be engaged to expedite the cases with regard to encroachment
and illegal/unauthorized constructions in the ASI protected monuments. (Para 37)
REGIONAL CENTRES OF NATIONAL SCHOOL OF DRAMA
The Committee is unable to comprehend the delay in granting the status of Institution of
National Importance to NSD. The Committee desires to receive a status report on the issue of
grant of the status of Institution of National Importance to the National School of Drama. The
Committee recommends that the opening of new Regional Centres of National School of Drama
should be carried on so as to facilitate the young people across the country to have access to such
great infrastructure and pursue their interest in the field. (Para 39)
PLAN ASSISTANCE FOR STATE AKADEMIS
The Committee observes that the Central Akademis can provide basic platform to the
State Akademis to work effectively at the grass root level to preserve and promote the diverse
cultural heritage of the country. The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry of Culture
is focusing some attention to the State Akademies which are in a poor financial condition. The
Committee recommends that the Ministry of Culture should devise some scheme specifically to
help the financial needs of the State level Akademis as they are a neglected lot at present.
(Para 41)
RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE HIGH POWERED COMMITTEE
The Committee appreciates that the Ministry has taken some initiatives towards implementing
the recommendations of the High Powered Committee and recommends that concerted steps
should be taken to implement the recommendations of the HPC so that the concerned cultural
institutions can be function efficiently and give optimum output. The latest status on the
implementation of HPC recommendations by various institutions may be furnished to the
Committee. (Para 43)
CELLULAR JAIL IN PORT BLAIR
The Committee is distressed to note that despite its repeated recommendations to include
the Cellular Jail in Port Blair in the World Heritage List of UNESCO, nothing concrete has been
done in this regard. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should furnish a status report
on the issue at the earliest and keeping in view of the historical importance of the Cellular Jail,
the Ministry of Culture should take proactive steps to include the Cellular Jail in Port Blair in
the World Heritage List of UNESCO. (Para 45)
The Committee has noted that proper data and documentation of history of Cellular Jail
in Port Blair has not been maintained. The Committee therefore recommends that steps should

30
be taken to maintain authentic data and avoid any misrepresentation of a place of historical
importance. (Para 46)
VACANCIES EXISTING IN VARIOUS ORGANIZATIONS OF THE MINISTRY
The Committee takes serious note of more than 2800 existing vacancies in ASI and desires
to be apprised of the effect of such a gap in staff strength and its adverse impact to maintain
the historical monuments in the country by ASI and the losses. When a large number of youths
are unemployed in our country it is cruel on the part of the Ministry of Culture and ASI to keep
thousands of posts vacant. Keeping in view the importance of ASI the Committee recommends
that every possible effort should be made to fill the vacancies in an expeditious manner.
(Para 50)
The Committee takes cognizance of the unfilled senior level vacancies existing in various
Organizations of the Ministry of Culture and desires to be apprised of as to how these organizations
are functioning without such senior level people. The Committee desires to be apprised of the
outcome with regard to the steps taken to fill all these vacancies so far. The Committee urges
upon the Ministry that the Recruitment Rules and other related matters should be finalized well
in advance in co-ordination with the concerned authorities. (Para 52)
CONSTRUCTION OF KOMAGATA MARU MEMORIAL
The Committee is happy to note the progress made towards construction of Komagata
Maru Memorial. The Committee desires that the Ministry should monitor the construction of the
Komagata Maru Memorial and apprise the Committee of the progress made in this regard.
(Para 54)
CULTURAL MAPPING OF INDIA
Cultural mapping embraces a broad definition of cultural resources which includes a wide
range of tangible resources such as arts and heritage organizations, cultural occupations and
industries, cultural and natural heritage -among others. It also explores the areas of intangible
cultural assets - the stories, traditions and unique quality of life that shape our identity and
sense of place. It is a dynamic concept. It will help in building better information on the cultural
assets in our country. A cultural asset inventory will be created, i.e., the project will produce a
baseline database of cultural resources in the country. The Committee recommends that
committees may be formed in different parts of the country to provide input and advice to the
mapping project. These committees may be comprised of a wide cross section of rural, urban,
municipal, cultural, business and community representatives and interests so that Cultural
Policy to provide a broad framework to support cultural planning and cultural development may
be framed. (Para 56)
The Committee notes there was a gross underutilisation of fund allocated to Cultural
Mapping programmes. The Committee feels the Government could not plan and structure the
programmes effectively which resulted in underutilisation of funds. The Committee may be

31
apprised of the reasons for underutilization and steps may be taken to utilize the money fully
in 2018-19. (Para 57)
NATIONAL MISSION ON LIBRARIES
The Committee is happy to note that Development of Libraries and Archives got ````` 99.81
crore in BE 2018-19 which is 100% increase in budget allocation in comparison to 2017-18. The
Committee while recognizing the importance of National Mission on Libraries desires to have a
progress report on the creation of National Virtual Library of India (NVLI). The Committee also
wants to be apprised of the utilization of fund allocated so far. The Committee recommends that
the work related to the schemes under National Mission on Libraries should be completed within
the extended time provided and accordingly, necessary steps should be taken. (Para 59)
The Committee also desires to have a status report on the progress of the work done under
the NML Model Libraries scheme. The Committee recommends that the work under this Scheme
should be expedited as libraries play a very crucial role in building the nation. (Para 60)
The Committee is impressed by the information that under the capacity building programme
about 2100 library professionals would be trained on modern techniques of library services and
application of ICT in modernization of library services. However, the Committee wants to know
whether infrastructure is available to train professionals in such a large scale. The Committee
recommends that steps must be taken well in advance to create infrastructure and formulate
plan to train such a large number of library professionals. (Para 61)
NATIONAL CULTURE FUND
The Committee recommends that the ongoing projects under NCF should be monitored in
regular intervals and the working of the Project Implementation Committee for each project
should also be scrutinized regularly so that delay and pendency can be avoided by timely sorting
out of problems. (Para 63)
KALA SANSKRITI VIKAS YOJANA
The Committee notes that under the head Kala Sanskriti Vikas Yojana out of ````` 310.48
crore at BE 2017-18 there was a reduction of ````` 60 cores at RE 2017-18 which definitely points
to bad planning and execution of projects under the Yojana. The Ministry has not given any
reasons for less expenditure on various programme under the Yojana. The Committee may be
apprised of the reasons for reduction at RE stage and actual utilization of funds under the Yojana
in 2017-18. The Committee hopes that the Ministry will take all efforts towards full utilization
of the allocation in 2018-19. (Para 65)
The Committee appreciates the activities undertaken in Kaka Sanskriti Vikas Yojana and
recommends that the Ministry should monitor each activity diligently and ensure optimum
utilization of allocated funds. The Ministry should actively pursue for extra budgetary provision
at RE 2018-19 as per requirement. (Para 66)

32
ARTISTS PENSION SCHEME AND WELFARE FUND
The Committee notes that the amount allocated under the Scheme has not been utilized
fully for the last three years. The Committee may be apprised of the reasons for such
underutilisation. (Para 68)
The Committee notes that out of the 1625 artistes selected for financial assistance, 1122
are from three states viz. Odisha, Maharashtra and Telengana. The Committee notes that there
is no relation between the number of applications considered and total number finally selected
for financial assistance. For instance in case of Odisha out of 464 application considered, 435
were selected for assistance whereas in case of Karnataka out of the 726 application considered
only 122 were selected for financial assistance. In some cases all the applications considered were

of selection for giving financial assistance. The Committee therefore recommends that it may
be provided with the criteria for selection of artistes for providing financial assistance. The
Committee urges that the Ministry should take care while selecting the artists and it should
represent the whole country uniformly. (Para 70)
The Committee is happy to note that an increased number of beneficiaries have been
recommended for financial assistance. However, the Committee wants to be apprised of the rules/
guidelines followed in recommending such beneficiaries. The Committee recommends that the
contributions of the artistes should be valued and they should be provided financial assistance
without creating a cumbersome process under the Artistes Pension Scheme. The Committee
would also like to know the amount that is being disbursed to artists under the Scheme.
(Para 71)
The Committee takes note of the initiative and recommends that concerted efforts in the
right direction should be an ongoing process. (Para 73)
GLOBAL ENGAGEMENT & INTERNATIONAL CO-OPERATION
The Committee takes note of the initiative. The Committee desires that the effectiveness
and usefulness of various festivals of India may be studied and reviewed to ensure that the
money is spend for useful purpose. (Para 76)
NATIONAL MISSION FOR PRESERV ATION OF MANUSCRIPTS
The Committee notes that the National Mission for preservation of Manuscripts is not
getting the attention required from the Government. Though there was a fund allocation of

The Committee has noted that the southern part of the country is totally neglected in
